paraphrase: Near the city's great cremation ground stands the Cāmuṇḍā called Karālā, said to delight in offerings of living beings; the powerful Kapālakuṇḍalā, disciple of Aghoraghaṇṭa - a night-roaming adept come from Śrīparvata who bears skulls and lives in the nearby forest - comes there every evening.
notes: Opponent's / outsider's report: Bhavabhūti's drama, portraying Kāpālikas as villains. checked against the local e-text in sources_raw; prose of act 1.

paraphrase: Aghoraghaṇṭa, his mantra-rite complete, has ordered that a jewel of a woman long promised to the goddess Karālā be offered that night; the two Kāpālikas worship Cāmuṇḍā and are about to kill Mālatī when Mādhava, who had come to the cremation ground to sell 'great flesh' to its spirits, intervenes and kills Aghoraghaṇṭa.
notes: Opponent's / outsider's report: Bhavabhūti's drama, portraying Kāpālikas as villains. checked against the local e-text in sources_raw; act 5.

paraphrase: Kapālakuṇḍalā, arriving through the air, praises the Lord of the Śaktis, encircled by Śaktis, whose self dwells in the middle of the circle of sixteen channels, whose form is placed in the heart, who grants powers to those who know him, sought by adepts of unwavering mind; she says that, seeing the self in Śiva's form in the heart-lotus of the six-limbed wheel, she has come, drawing up the 'five nectars' of the world through the rising order of the channels, without the fatigue of flight, parting the clouds before her.
